newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Bund futures fall after Buba announcement.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Bund futures fall after Buba announcement.

text.p: German Bund futures at the Chicago Board of Trade fell in afternoon trade after news that the Bundesbank rejected a government asset revaluation plan.
The Bundesbank issued a statement Wednesday afternoon rejecting German government plans to revalue its gold and currency reserves.
The German coalition government said it would continue with the plan to revalue Bundesbank reserves.
A trader for a Wall Street firm called the news "an interesting development."
"The bottom line is there is a good rift developing between the Bundesbank and the government, and you sell Bunds on that."
He said trading volume picked up on the Bundesbank-Bonn dispute, but said overall action was only moderate and the tone choppy.
"We saw heavy selling by a number of different firms," said Kurt Fraim, vice president with Aubrey G. Lanston.

"It's nice to see that there is an opportunity for trade after London closes," Fraim added, referring to the recent linkage between the CBOT and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange.
At the close, June Bund futures were down 0.20 point at 100.50, after trading in a range from 100.45 to 101.02.
